question_text: Write the difference between actin and myosin.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Actin
steps.why: The thin filament is anchored at the Z line, which is why the light band is where actin alone lies.
common_mistakes: Calling actin the thick filament. It is thin.
Attaching actin to the M line. It attaches to the Z line.
steps.memory_tip: Actin is thin, in the light band, tied to the Z line.
steps.margin_note: Three points each, written side by side.
lines: Actin is a thin contractile protein.
It lies in the light band, the isotropic
Actin filaments are attached to the Z line.

steps.label: Myosin
steps.why: The thick filament fills the dark band, so the band looks dark exactly where myosin lies.
common_mistakes: Putting myosin in the light band. It is in the dark band.
Attaching myosin to the Z line. It attaches to the M line.
steps.memory_tip: Myosin is thick, in the dark band, tied to the M line.
steps.margin_note: Keep the same order of points as for actin.
lines: Myosin is a thick contractile protein.
It lies in the dark band, the anisotropic

lines.text: Myosin filaments are attached to the M line

insider_note: Write it as two columns. A difference question answered as a paragraph is hard to mark and usually loses one of the two marks.
